Institutions and languages

75 directory entries = 36 banks + 14 broker/DP labels + 25 mutual funds. These are searchable starting points. They are not 75 integrations or individually verified workflows. Custom institutions can also be recorded.

6 institutions have curated guidance, with 7 reference routes: HDFC Bank, SBI, Axis Bank, Zerodha, Groww and HDFC Mutual Fund. Applicability depends on product, holding and requested action; other cases receive clearly labelled general guidance.

From one account to a family that is prepared

Small steps. Lasting family confidence.

Virasat connects the steps that are easy to lose between services: find the right route, prepare the request, check the result and leave a usable family record.

Potential impact · illustrative 90-day scenario · 1,000 eligible cases

+220

Additional confirmations

About 620 completed confirmations versus an assumed 400 through usual help: 55% more in this scenario.

+305

Additional family-ready records

About 465 usable family records versus an assumed 160. Confirmation and family readiness are connected outcomes.

500 hours

Less active effort

Thirty minutes less per case: one-third less effort, with more time for the family.

What a 10,000-case programme could enable

At the same assumed rates: 2,200 additional confirmations, 3,050 additional family-ready records and 5,000 hours less active effort. This is a tenfold scenario, not a verified programme result.

How the scenario is calculated

Illustrative assumptions for 1,000 eligible securities nomination cases over 90 days: 90% start × 90% correct route × 85% submission × 90% confirmation = 619.65 confirmations. Assumed comparison: 40% confirmation = 400. Difference: 219.65, displayed as 220; relative increase: 54.9%, displayed as 55%.

Family readiness assumes 75% of scenario confirmations versus 40% of comparison confirmations: 464.7375 versus 160, a difference of 304.7375, displayed as 305. This overlaps confirmations and must not be added to them. Active effort assumes 60 versus 90 minutes per enrolled case, giving 500 hours less. The 10,000-case numbers use exact tenfold arithmetic rounded for presentation.

These are planning assumptions, not measured user outcomes or estimates calibrated from public statistics. No user trials have been run; money recovered and visits avoided are unmeasured. Institution acceptance, user completion and recipient readiness determine the actual outcome. The downloadable register includes the model and a sensitivity case.

A branch visit, prepared in one place

4 preparation outputs in 1 pack, available in 21 text languages. Where to go, what to bring, what to ask and what confirmation to keep. Print or save as PDF using the browser, or download a standalone HTML copy that opens without an internet connection. Private notes and nominee names stay out of the pack.

21 of 21 translated fixture packs fit on one A4 page. Checked in desktop Chrome 138 with 12 mm margins and browser headers off. Download sizes in this joint-account fixture range from 4,239 to 23,495 bytes, including embedded fonts where needed. Official websites still need a connection. This checks print layout, not language fluency or institutional acceptance.

Older-phone target and verification status

Device target: all app functions on an eight-year-old Android phone with 2 GB RAM and a 3G connection.

Design target — not verified on a matching physical phone. No matching phone or real-device account is available. Desktop CPU/heap limits and mobile viewports do not reproduce phone age, total RAM or Android behaviour.

Verified wording: “The app completed 12 cold desktop lab starts with 8× CPU slowdown, including a 160 kbps / 800 ms response-body profile. The inspected confirmation form worked at 320px width and 200% text.”

An old Android phone needs a compatible browser, ES modules, native dialogs and Web Crypto. Current Chrome needs Android 10+; Chrome 138 was the last version supporting Android 8/9. Chrome requirements · Older Android support.

Additional older-engine tests

Chrome 138: 52 core checks passed in each of three runs. These include account transitions, private correction handling, 21 text packs and audio routing, plus encryption/restoration of the maximum 50-account fixture. These are exported-logic/API checks, not all rendered UI functions.

Three cold Hindi starts in the same desktop engine reached controls ready in a median 2.90 seconds, with 106,738 bytes of navigation transfer. Conditions: 384 kbps response bodies, 200 ms fixed request latency, 8× host-relative CPU slowdown and 64 MiB V8 old-space cap. These use UMTS/3G download magnitudes, not a full cellular-radio simulation.

This is desktop Chrome 138 on macOS. Lighthouse's mobile user-agent string does not turn it into Android. It does not verify 2 GB phone RAM, an eight-year-old CPU, print/file-picker behaviour or real audio playback. Measured snapshot: ba43e3703ffae66e90633cca7b6a170f75241be1509bdf436982fe8f250f613f.

Credible tools investigated

  • BrowserStack Live real devices: Real-device network simulation requires an eligible account/plan; exact old 2 GB handset availability must be confirmed. No session was run.
  • Android official emulator: Virtual RAM and UMTS/3G network settings; useful Android compatibility evidence, not a physical handset performance result. No emulator test was run.
  • WebPageTest: Current mobile FAQ recommends browser emulation. A mobile viewport alone cannot verify 2 GB hardware.
  • LambdaTest / TestMu network testing: Network profiles for supported test environments; verify device, account and plan capabilities before claiming a real-phone result.
  • Google Chrome for Testing: Pinned older desktop Chrome can validate that engine; it cannot establish Android or total-phone memory performance.

Technical evidence, data and bounds

Latest journey review · 4 October 2026

167 release checks passed; 0 failures. The redesigned app completed three cold Hindi starts in desktop Chrome 138 with controls ready in a median 2.82 seconds, transferring 111,342 bytes per start. Measured layout shift: 0 in all three runs.

Conditions: 384 kbps response bodies, 200 ms fixed request latency, 360 × 800 mobile viewport, 8× host-relative CPU slowdown and 64 MiB V8 old-space cap. These are desktop lab results; the matching Android phone remains untested. Earlier measurements below retain their original snapshots. Latest measured source: 625f2a7e7c7516b12fc4444fdab53807b4871751d821c68226e37682081699eb.

Product, reading and encryption numbers
  • Three account categories. The prototype allows up to four bank nominee notes or three securities nominee notes per account; these are recording limits, not institutional eligibility decisions.
  • Text size: 90–200%; primary controls: at least 44 CSS pixels. Listening speeds: 0.75×, 0.9× and 1.05×.
  • Personal review: one year. SCORES reminders: 15 days from the relevant report receipt, with separate first and second stages; official instructions govern action.
  • Encrypted saves: AES-256-GCM; PBKDF2-SHA256 with 600,000 iterations. Password length: 12–256 characters. Passwords are not retained; there is no password recovery.

The figures below refer to the measured Babulal build before this evidence-page addition. Public source SHA-256: 2b255a132d85daaa9ea915c463e9d3328de6e3cdde07da47d82dc1ff00857491. This English page loads only when opened; it is not part of the account application's eager asset set.

160 release tests passed. Final axe-core 4.13.0 scans found zero violations and zero unresolved checks on inspected home/confirmation screens. At 320 × 800 pixels, 200% text, high contrast and extra spacing, the confirmation had no app-element overflow. This is not WCAG/GIGW certification or a screen-reader study.

Paper HTML alone: English 1,595 bytes gzip; Hindi 2,308 bytes gzip. Shared CSS/font is additional. All 4,960 supplemental files decoded without error; understandability is untested.

The full public catalog totals 238,855,244 bytes, mostly audio. Visitors do not download it all. Public shell cache: 8 MiB. Shared audio cache: 12 MiB / 256 entries. Browser eviction can remove offline content.

Private limits: 50 accounts; 20 nomination events and 20 support events per account; 1 MiB plaintext save; 2 MiB import. Maximum synthetic fixture: 542,316 bytes plaintext and 723,275 bytes encrypted, restored exactly in three desktop Node crypto runs. No Android import or tab-eviction result is claimed.

Nine loopback static-server runs completed 99,802 requests with zero reported errors. This is not production or concurrent-human-user capacity. Arithmetic only: one million independent cold Hindi text loads at the measured gzip inventory would be 97.576 GB before overhead. Assuming 1 MiB audio per session adds 1,048.576 GB. Neither scenario verifies hosting capacity or adoption.
